places.name: Alcaraz Flats High School
places.description: A 2,100-student campus of tan stucco wings on Vinca Avenue, home of the Egrets. The football stadium has aluminum bleachers that burn your legs in August.

places.name: Tamsen Valley College
places.description: A hillside community college with a nursing prep program and a 7 a.m. parking scramble in Lot C. Many students work warehouse nights and take afternoon classes.

places.name: Bayshore State University, Tamsen campus
places.description: A nearby campus of the state university system twenty minutes north on the Tule Line, known for its nursing and logistics management programs. Transfer students from Tamsen Valley fill its evening sections.

places.name: St. Anselm Valley Medical Center
places.description: A 280-bed hospital on Ortega Hill with a crowded ER and a new tower still smelling of paint. Nurses park in a gravel overflow lot and take a shuttle.

places.name: Calle Ortega
places.description: Six blocks of old storefronts, taquerias, a shuttered theater and a tax-prep office. String lights cross the street between the 1920s brick buildings.

places.name: Ridgeline Freight Fulfillment Center RF-4
places.description: A 900,000-square-foot gray warehouse on Ruel Road running three shifts and 140 truck doors. Workers scan totes on handhelds that beep red when you fall behind rate.

places.name: Marisol Gardens Apartments
places.description: A 1970s two-story complex with a cracked pool, 180 units and a laundry room that takes cards only since spring.

places.name: Verdant Commons
places.description: A new five-story podium building next to Flats Junction with a rooftop grill and $2,900 one-bedrooms. Package lockers overflow every Monday.

places.name: Ruiz Family Market
places.description: An independent grocery on Vinca with a carnicería counter, a fresh tortilla machine and fish sauce in aisle 6.

places.name: Flats Junction Station
places.description: The Tule Line stop with a 400-space lot full by 7:10 a.m. and a coffee cart under the canopy.

places.name: Taquería Colima
places.description: A Calle Ortega counter spot with $3.25 al pastor tacos and a line of warehouse workers after the 6 p.m. shift change.

places.name: Phở Bến Thành
places.description: A strip-mall pho house with laminated menus and a big tank of iced tea; nurses come in after night shift at 8 a.m.

places.name: Heron & Grind
places.description: A cafe in a former bank on Calle Ortega with outlets along the vault wall, popular with college students studying.

places.name: Cloud Nine Tea Bar
places.description: A boba shop in Plaza Marisol where high schoolers crowd in after 3:15 and order taro slush.

places.name: Plaza Marisol
places.description: A strip mall with a nail salon, dentist, phone repair shop, pho house and a big parking lot where teens hang out.

places.name: Iron Flats Fitness
places.description: A 24-hour gym in an old auto parts store, $29 a month, busiest at 5 a.m. and midnight with shift workers.

places.name: Ulloa Salt Marsh Park
places.description: A marsh park with a boardwalk trail, egrets and a playground; the trail floods at king tides.

places.name: Delgado Park
places.description: The town's central park with soccer fields, a bandstand and the Sunday farmers market lot.

places.name: Alcaraz Flats Public Library, Main Branch
places.description: A low brick library with a busy homework center, free printing up to 20 pages and a seed library by the door.

places.name: Our Lady of the Marsh Parish
places.description: A white stucco Catholic church with Masses in English, Spanish and Tagalog and a food pantry on Thursdays.

places.name: Sikh Gurdwara of Tamsen Valley
places.description: A gurdwara on Pell Road serving free langar every Sunday; warehouse drivers stop in for chai.

places.name: Vinca Avenue Community Center
places.description: A 1980s rec center hosting senior lunches, ESL classes, polling and candidate forums in its multipurpose room.

places.name: Suds City Laundromat
places.description: A 24-hour laundromat on Vinca where a double load costs $6.50 and a TV plays telenovelas.

places.name: Panadería Las Hermanas
places.description: A Calle Ortega bakery with conchas at $1.50 and a line out the door Saturday mornings.

places.name: Kessler Middle School
places.description: A middle school across from Delgado Park whose drop-off line overlaps with the high school's.

places.name: Ruel Road Industrial Corridor
places.description: A strip of warehouses, truck yards and a cheap gas station along Ruel Road, full of potholes and diesel smell.

places.name: Ortega Playhouse
places.description: A restored 1928 theater on Calle Ortega used by community groups and the high school's fall play.

places.name: Grace's home
places.description: three-bedroom ranch house on Tamarisk Court, owned with Ramón since 2009

places.name: Jun's home
places.description: his childhood bedroom in Tess's house off Vinca Avenue

places.name: Jun's home

places.name: Linh's home

places.name: Rafael's home

places.name: Rochelle's home

events.title: First day at Alcaraz Flats High
events.description: Students return for the fall semester; parents juggle early drop-off with shifts and Vinca traffic backs up.

events.title: Tamsen Valley College fall term begins
events.description: Classes start; Lot C overflows and working students scramble to add classes around warehouse shifts.

events.title: Late-summer heat wave
events.description: Highs over 100°F; Ridgeline adds water breaks, the ER sees heat cases, schools hold minimum days, the library opens as a cooling center.

events.title: Labor Day
events.description: Schools and college closed; Ridgeline pays holiday time-and-a-half to those working; families picnic at Delgado Park.

events.title: Egrets home football opener
events.description: Friday night game drawing students, families and off-shift workers to the stadium.

events.title: Ridgeline peak-season hiring fair
events.description: Ridgeline hires 400 seasonal workers at $21.75; college students and parents line up early.

events.title: St. Anselm goes live with new charting system
events.description: Nurses and doctors switch to a new electronic charting system; overtime spikes and patients see longer waits.

events.title: Calle Ortega Street Fair
events.description: Street closed for food stalls, live music and local vendors; families and teens crowd the downtown blocks.

events.title: Delgado Park harvest farmers market
events.description: Sunday market with stone fruit, peppers and tamales; seniors and families shop after church.

events.title: Ridgeline mandatory overtime begins
events.description: Ten-hour shifts and a new scanner quota; workers juggle childcare and classes and the gym fills at odd hours.

events.title: City council candidate forum
events.description: Candidates debate warehouse growth, housing and Measure K; residents line up to ask questions.

events.title: Indigenous Peoples' Day
events.description: Schools closed; the library hosts a storytelling program and families visit the marsh park.

events.title: Tamsen Valley College midterms
events.description: Students cram at Heron & Grind and the library, many after overtime shifts.

events.title: St. Anselm nurses union vote
events.description: Nurses vote on unionizing over staffing ratios; families of patients and hospital workers watch closely.

events.title: Egrets homecoming game
events.description: Homecoming football and court; students, alumni and families pack the stadium.

events.title: Halloween on Calle Ortega
events.description: Merchants hand out candy; kids trick-or-treat downtown and in Marisol Gardens.

events.title: Local election and Measure K
events.description: Residents vote on council seats and Measure K; polling at the community center.

events.title: Flats High fall play
events.description: Students perform at the Ortega Playhouse; families attend.

events.title: Veterans Day ceremony
events.description: Schools closed; ceremony at Delgado Park bandstand attended by veterans and families.

events.title: First fall storm
events.description: Heavy rain floods the marsh trail and Ruel Road; commuters face Tule Line delays and the ER sees crash injuries.

events.title: Flats High semester midterms
events.description: Students study at the library homework center and boba shop.

events.title: Thanksgiving food drive
events.description: Parish and gurdwara volunteers distribute turkeys and groceries to families.

lines.what: First day at Flats High: Dulce walks the 12 minutes down Vinca through the backed-up drop-off line and gets her schedule: geometry, English 10, chemistry with Ms. Tolentino, history, PE, Spanish.
Third period chemistry with Ms. Tolentino; she is paired with Karina as lab partner. PE starts with a volleyball unit.
Lunch at the planters by the B wing with Brianna, Karina and Sienna, swapping schedules and complaining about early drop-off.
At home in unit 114 she tells her mom Yesenia about the day and sorts through the stack of syllabi.
School day: geometry numbers come easily, and Ms. Tolentino hands out the lab safety sheet. Principal Ocampo's attendance push means teachers are tracking who is absent.
After school she fills out the work permit form for the taquería and gets it ready for the school office.
Evening homework at the kitchen table; she finishes geometry fast but leaves English reading for later.
Heat wave begins and the school runs a minimum day; Dulce walks home in 100-degree heat.
Picks up the school-issued work permit from the office. It limits her to 18 hours on school weeks.
Cools off at home with the fan on and texts the group chat about the heat and her first shift.
Another minimum day in the heat. Chemistry is a short lab-safety review, and the B wing planters are too hot, so lunch moves into the shade.
Yesenia gives her a quick rundown of how to take the 22 bus down Calle Ortega for work tomorrow.
Lays out her black shirt for tomorrow and does a little geometry homework, then goes to bed.
School in the heat, then the 22 bus down Calle Ortega. Efraín shows her the register and the ticket pen rule, and Camila walks her through orders.
Eats her free quesadilla on break, and Héctor teases her about slow tickets. She learns paychecks come every other Friday by check and opens a phone fund goal of $220.
Rafael picks her up after the 9 p.m. close in the heat-warm night. She asks for help wording a thank-you text, worried it sounds cringe.
Saturday laundry at the card-only room at Marisol Gardens while the heat wave lingers.
Takes a break at the library, which is open as a cooling center, and gets a start on English reading.
Evening video chat with the girls about first-week gossip, and she works on an edit video she never posts.
Sunday 10-4 shift at Taquería Colima after the 22 bus. She takes lunch rush orders and gets quicker at the register.
She counts the hours worked so far against the permit's 18-hour limit and tells her mom how much her first check might be.
Evening homework and an early bedtime before Monday classes.
Labor Day: no school. Dulce sleeps in, then walks over to Delgado Park with Yesenia for the family picnic crowd and bandstand music.
Back at Marisol Gardens she counts her first paycheck money out loud and moves it toward the phone fund.
Walks the 12 minutes down Vinca to Flats High. Gets through geometry and English, then chemistry third period with Ms. Tolentino, sitting by Karina.
Evening at home, texts in the 'las 4' chat and watches edit videos she never posts.
School day with world history, PE volleyball and Spanish for heritage speakers. Eats lunch with Brianna, Karina and Sienna.
Does geometry homework at the kitchen table fast, then fumbles the chem lab writeup.
Classes as usual; Eli shares chem notes from behind her. She helps fold to-go boxes? No, saves that for later and goes home after school.
Yesenia reminds her of the 9:30 school-night curfew and the shift tomorrow. Dulce picks out her work shirt.
After school, Dulce takes the 22 bus down Calle Ortega for her 4-9 Friday shift at Taquería Colima, taking orders next to Camila with Héctor's rancheras on the radio.

Before the shift, she stops at Cloud Nine Tea Bar with Brianna, Karina and Sienna on the way to the football opener crowd. The receipt comes to $31 and she decides to just pay it all so it's not weird.
Efraín closes at 9 and Rafael picks her up in his car; they hear the football opener horns from the stadium.
Saturday laundry at the card-only laundry room in Marisol Gardens.
Drops by the pupusa stand to say hi to Tía Gladys and Rafael, and takes a pupusa.
Evening of scrolling and chatting in the group chat; hears Brianna talk about plans for her birthday.
Takes the 22 bus to Taquería Colima for her Sunday 10-4 shift, working the register through the lunch rush.
Home after work, she checks her phone fund and starts her Monday chem homework.
Winds down with K-pop playlists and sleeps by 11:30.
Dulce walks the 12 minutes down Vinca to Flats High for geometry and English, then sits through Ms. Tolentino's third-period chemistry with Karina as lab partner.
Eats lunch at the planters by the B wing with Brianna, Karina and Sienna, then goes home to Marisol Gardens unit 114 for homework.
Texts in 'las 4 fantásticas' late and falls asleep a bit after 11:30.
School day: geometry, chemistry, PE volleyball unit. Dulce is quick at the molar mass practice problems.
After school she and friends stop at Cloud Nine Tea Bar, where Kyla gives extra pearls, and Dulce orders a taro slush.
Home by curfew; Yesenia gets home from her St. Anselm shift and they eat dinner together.
Wednesday classes: English 10, world history and Spanish for heritage speakers.
Eats lunch at the B wing planters with the group and works on the chem lab conclusion afterward.
Chats with friends at night and edits a video clip she will never post.
Thursday at school with chemistry third period, then a bus and a walk home.
Evening at home with homework while Yesenia cooks; Dulce checks her phone fund total and counts it out.
Phone battery dies before dinner, so she charges it while doing geometry.
Friday at school, then a 22 bus ride down Calle Ortega to Taquería Colima for her 4-9 shift taking orders.
Héctor jokes loudly at the grill during the rush and slows the ticket line; Dulce privately finds him a show-off.
After her check, Yesenia sets a rule: Dulce keeps her paycheck but puts $20 per check toward her phone bill. Rafael picks her up after the 9 p.m. close.
Saturday morning laundry at the card-only laundry room in Marisol Gardens.

Afternoon hanging out with friends at Plaza Marisol and she buys one round of boba.
Sunday 10-4 shift at Taquería Colima taking orders next to Camila and Héctor.
Takes her free shift plate, a quesadilla, then rides the 22 bus home.
Starts the week's chem homework and goes to bed on time.
Walks the 12 minutes down Vinca to Flats High, sits through geometry and English, and eats lunch at the B wing planters with Brianna, Karina and Sienna.
Evening at unit 114 with Yesenia, who is home by 3:30 from her St. Anselm shift. Dulce counts her phone fund out loud and checks her chat.
Third period chemistry with Ms. Tolentino: molar mass practice, lab partner Karina. Lunch is back at the planters.

Chemistry lab day. Dulce finishes the molar mass calculations in seconds but stalls on the lab conclusion.
At home that evening, Dulce asks the assistant to just tell her what a conclusion is supposed to say. The math part is already done.
School day, then Dulce does homework at the kitchen table in unit 114 and finishes the lab conclusion.
Dulce texts Karina about Saturday's street fair and sees the group chat go quiet, then comes back to jokes.
Fifth period PE volleyball, then the 22 bus to Calle Ortega for her 4-9 shift at Taquería Colima. Héctor's rancheras play behind the grill.
At close, Efraín lets Dulce count the drawer because she makes change faster than the register. She gets it to the penny on her own.

Saturday laundry at the card-only laundry room, then Dulce and Karina walk the Calle Ortega Street Fair, with food stalls, live music and a crowded Panadería Las Hermanas.

Evening at home; Dulce realizes the party clashes with her Sunday 10-4 shift and thinks about how to fix it.

Having said yes to both Camila and Brianna, Dulce asks the assistant to help write a message to Efraín explaining the swap.
Dulce goes to Brianna's birthday party and then home, where Yesenia is waiting.
Walks to Flats High along Vinca; at lunch by the B wing planters Brianna announces her breakup with Tyler and accuses Dulce of leaking it to Karina, while Sienna backs her up.

Eats dinner in Marisol Gardens unit 114 with her mom Yesenia and is home before the 9:30 curfew.
Skips the planters and eats lunch in Ms. Tolentino's room B12 with Karina and Eli, who shares notes from chem.
Third-period chemistry with Ms. Tolentino; Dulce does the mole calculations quickly beside Karina.
Takes the walk home alone, then does homework in the small bedroom by the laundry wall.
Finds she was removed from the 'las 4 fantásticas' chat and Karina adds her to a new chat, 'lab rats', with Eli.

Eats B12 lunch again, then goes home to eat dinner.
Walks to school and eats lunch in B12 with Karina and Eli.

Does Saturday laundry at the card-only laundry room at Marisol Gardens.
Hangs out in the 'lab rats' chat with Karina and Eli and edits a TikTok-style video she never posts.
Skips boba and has dinner with her mom.
Takes the 22 bus to Calle Ortega for her Sunday 10-4 shift at Taquería Colima.

Walks to Flats High on Vinca for a normal Monday, then eats lunch in Ms. Tolentino's room B12 with Karina and Eli.
Third-period chemistry with Ms. Tolentino; Dulce does the mole calculations fast but stalls on the lab conclusion.
Dinner with her mom Yesenia at unit 114 in Marisol Gardens, then geometry homework before bed.
School day: geometry first, then chemistry, then B12 lunch with Karina and Eli.

Chats with Karina late in the evening about nothing in particular before bed.

B12 lunch with Karina and Eli; Eli plays a bass line on his knee while they trade chem answers.

Lunch in B12 beforehand with Karina and Eli, acting normal.
School all day, then takes the 22 bus down Calle Ortega to Taquería Colima for her 4-9 Friday shift.

Sunday shift at Taquería Colima 10-4, ringing up the lunch crowd.

Group-chat banter in 'lab rats' with Karina and Eli, mostly memes, then bed.
School day, with lunch in B12 and chemistry third period with Ms. Tolentino.

Asked Ms. Lugo and her physics teacher Mr. Okafor to be her recommenders.
Thursday robotics in room C7, 3:30 to 6.

Lola Cora's sinigang for Sunday dinner; Isabel pretended not to care and had two bowls.

Home for dinner; Lola Cora's TV blares teleseryes while Isabel does dishes.

Evening review of her 600-card anatomy deck while lo-fi plays.

Home dinner at 8 with Hạnh, who asks about pharmacy classes; Linh gives short answers.

Evening at the library with her notes on the nervous system; pours a pour-over at home after.

Jun sells lumpia at the counter on Saturday under Beatrice's deal; Linh bags orders.
Afternoon studying the skeleton with blue notes, followed by phở leftovers at home.
Sunday shift 6:30 to 1 at Heron & Grind, then Lotus Nails front desk 2 to 5.
Walks the Ulloa marsh boardwalk, passing the farmers market crowd at Delgado Park on the way.
Preps rice bowls for the week and fills in her planner with washi tape.
Linh wakes at 6:45 and rides the Kenji-ride/shuttle route to Tamsen Valley for Anatomy with Dr. Okoye at 9, then skips lunch again until her shift.

Thao's boyfriend Tomás finishes moving into unit 207; Thao mentions it by text before her night shift.

Studies at home with the lo-fi playlist and her dad's old radio on the desk.

Works the 6:30-1 Sunday cafe shift, pouring hearts and practicing the rosetta between orders.
Helps at the Lotus Nails front desk from 2 to 5 for Hạnh.
Walks the Ulloa marsh boardwalk, then plans the week in her planner Sunday night.

Closed up, wrote milk waste on the clipboard, and went home to a plate from Hạnh.
Kenji gave her a ride to General Chemistry at 11 a.m., and she took color-coded notes.
Studied in the library afterward and skipped lunch until Kenji handed her half a sandwich.
Evening at home reviewing the yellow list for the practical.
Anatomy at 9 a.m. and a quiz review with Rochelle, who complained about online quizzes.
Spent the afternoon comparing used e-bike listings and messaged a seller about a $640 one.
Evening at home with Hạnh, who asked about pharmacy and Linh changed the subject to dinner.
Worked the Saturday 6:30-1 shift at Heron & Grind, with Sam taking the second register.
After work she bought the used e-bike for $640 and arranged to charge it behind the cafe counter.
Rode the e-bike home along Calle Ortega for the first time and ate dinner with Hạnh.
Sunday 6:30-1 shift at Heron & Grind, then rode the e-bike to Lotus Nails to work the front desk 2-5.
Walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk for a short stretch in the late afternoon fog.
Planned the week in her planner and asked her assistant for a day-by-day countdown to the practical on Oct 17, color-tagged to match her notes.
Indigenous Peoples' Day, no classes. Linh sleeps in, then works Monday at Heron & Grind from 3 to 9 closing, logging milk waste and locking the vault-room outlets.

Rides her new e-bike home from Calle Ortega after close and charges it in the hallway.

Annoyed that Beatrice docks the closers' tip jar for breakage, she drafts an email about it and asks whether she can just not send it. She doesn't send it.
Anatomy at 9 with Dr. Okoye on the eve of midterm week. Rochelle sits beside her cracking jokes about the practical.

Closing shift at Heron & Grind, 3 to 9, with midterm students crowding the vault-wall outlets until close. Wes isn't there, but she hears the cortado regulars called 'Doc' jokes from Jun.
Chemistry at 11, then a late-afternoon cram at the library the day before the practical. She skips lunch again.

Bed at 12:30 with her dad's radio on the desk and a lo-fi playlist, going over cranial nerves one last time.
Takes Dr. Okoye's first lab practical at 9, the one a third of each section fails.
Meets Thao at Phở Bến Thành after her night shift. Thao mentions the Ridgeline IT lead and charting news among the hospital gossip.

Lumpia Saturday at the counter; Jun sells trays under Beatrice's 15 percent deal while Linh handles the espresso rush.
Charges the e-bike behind the counter and rides home at 1 to nap.
Sunday cafe shift from 6:30 to 1, then a quick lunch from her prepped rice bowl.
Helps at the Lotus Nails front desk from 2 to 5 for Hạnh.
Walks the Ulloa marsh boardwalk, then plans the week in her paper planner before the chemistry midterm on Monday at 8.
Up at 6:45 and biked to Tamsen Valley for the 8 a.m. General Chemistry midterm, then sat in anatomy at 9 next to Rochelle.

Got home after 9:30 and ate the plate Hạnh left out, then reviewed flashcards in bed.
Rode with Kenji to campus for General Chemistry at 11, the last day of midterm week, and ate her packed rice bowl between classes.
Went to Pedro's Tuesday 4 p.m. anatomy group at the library and quizzed with his bone models.
Planned the week in her paper planner with washi tape and made a lo-fi playlist for studying.
Anatomy at 9 with Dr. Okoye, who said practical grades would be posted Friday.
Worked the Wednesday 3-9 closing shift at Heron & Grind, charging her e-bike behind the counter. Wes called her 'Doc' at the afternoon rush.
Rode home in the dark and finished a flashcard deck review before bed.
General Chemistry at 11, with a ride from Kenji. Thao texted that the St. Anselm nurses union vote was happening and she'd be at the hospital.
Studied at Heron & Grind on her day off from the counter, using the vault-wall outlets.
Ate dinner with Hạnh, who asked again about pharmacy; Linh steered the talk to the salon.
Anatomy at 9: Dr. Okoye posted the practical grades and Linh got a 91, putting her at an A- overall. She asked whether a 91 was good enough and whether the class average was posted.
Told Pedro and Rochelle her score at lunch, and Rochelle cheered her on.
Stayed home on homecoming night while the stadium filled up, and texted Kenji about the A-.
Opened Heron & Grind at 6:30 for the Saturday shift, with Jun selling lumpia at the counter.
Got Sam to cover her last hour since she owed him nothing; he still owes her two Saturdays.
Made a Sunday-prep list and shopped for rice bowl ingredients at Ruiz Family Market, where Kenji rang her up.
Worked the Sunday 6:30-1 shift at Heron & Grind.
Staffed the front desk at Lotus Nails from 2 to 5 for Hạnh.
Walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk in the late afternoon, then planned the week in her planner and prepped rice bowls.

Linh rode her e-bike to Tamsen Valley for Anatomy at 9 a.m. and sat through the digestion lecture next to Rochelle. Afterward she looked up extra reading on the gut microbiome, though no test covers it.
Closing shift at Heron & Grind from 3 to 9, charging the e-bike behind the counter, logging milk waste and locking the vault-room outlets.
Kenji gave her a ride to General Chemistry at 11. She spent the afternoon at the library with Pedro's Tuesday 4 p.m. anatomy group.
Evening at home on Pell Road, she packed tomorrow's rice bowl and updated her color-coded notes and planner.
Linh had Anatomy at 9 a.m., then met counselor Denny Wu at 2 p.m. They drafted a two-track plan: Bayshore nursing versus Bayshore public health, with the decision due by February.
Closing shift at the cafe from 3 to 9. Between rushes she told Jun about the plan but kept it vague.
General Chemistry at 11, with Kenji driving her. Afterward she reviewed her anatomy deck on the library steps.
Evening of studying at home to lo-fi, then dinner with Hạnh.
Halloween shift at Heron & Grind, working the whole day to closing. She drew skeleton latte art, and Calle Ortega filled with trick-or-treaters.
Closed the cafe, logged milk waste, and biked home past the street's string lights.
Opening shift at Heron & Grind at 6:30 a.m. Sam was supposed to help but swapped out again.
Got off at 1 and ate her packed rice bowl. Spent the afternoon on chemistry problem sets at the vault-wall outlets.
Evening at home, she planned next week in her washi-tape planner.
Sunday cafe shift from 6:30 to 1, then a walk on the Ulloa marsh boardwalk.
Helped at the Lotus Nails front desk from 2 to 5 with Hạnh.
Sunday night she set up her weekly planner and prepped rice bowls.

Worked the Monday 3-9 closing shift at Heron & Grind, logging milk waste and locking the vault-room outlets. Jun asked about the next lumpia numbers.
Heard from Thao that Hana started back full time at Bayshore State admissions today. Linh wrote her Sunday-night planner notes into the week.
Linh had General Chemistry at 11 a.m. and got a ride from Kenji. Election day signs filled the Vinca Avenue corner by the community center.
Attended Pedro's Tuesday 4 p.m. anatomy group at the library, quizzing with his bone models.
Evening at home with a pour-over and color-coded notes while Hạnh talked about Measure K at dinner.
Anatomy at 9 a.m. with Rochelle beside her, then a bike-less day of shuttle rides across campus.
Signed up to help sort at the Nov 22 food drive at Our Lady of the Marsh, then worked the 3-9 closing shift at Heron & Grind.
Chemistry at 11 a.m. with a ride from Kenji, then lunch from her Sunday-prepped rice bowl.
Studied at the library after class, reviewing the 600-card anatomy deck on breaks.
Dinner at home; Hạnh asked about pharmacy and Linh changed the subject.
Anatomy at 9 a.m., then quiz review at the library with Pedro's group notes.
Spent Friday afternoon on Statistics online homework at Heron & Grind, sitting by the vault wall while Jun worked the bar.
Evening at home; Flats High fall play opened at the Ortega Playhouse and Calle Ortega was busy with families.

Jun sold lumpia at the counter on Saturday under Beatrice's deal, and Linh helped him tally sales.
Shift ended at 1 p.m. and she went home to rest, then wrote notes for the week ahead.
Sunday shift at Heron & Grind from 6:30 to 1.
Worked the front desk at Lotus Nails from 2 to 5 with Hạnh.
Walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk in the late afternoon fog, then planned the week in her paper planner with washi tape.

Before her Monday shift at Heron & Grind she catches Thao at the apartment after a night shift and tells her she is considering a public health or nutrition transfer instead of pharmacy. She goes to Thao before anyone else because Thao is the one who will not freak out.
Closing shift at Heron & Grind, Mon 3-9, logging milk waste and locking the vault-room outlets; Jun jokes about her latte art.

Dinner at home on Pell Road with Hạnh, who talks about salon customers; Linh says nothing about the pharmacy talk.
Anatomy with Dr. Okoye at 9, sitting beside Rochelle, then a quick flashcard review before heading to work.
Closing shift at Heron & Grind, Wed 3-9; Wes calls her Doc as he stops in for a late tea.

Sunday shift at Heron & Grind 6:30-1, then helps at Lotus Nails' front desk from 2 to 5.

Sunday planning night with her washi-tape planner, laying out the week and registration morning.

Biked home on the e-bike she charged behind the counter and left a note for Hạnh about Thursday's dinner.

Called Thao before her night shift to say goodnight and ask about phở on the weekend.

Lunch with Kenji at Heron & Grind's vault-wall outlets, where he studied for his transfer app.
Sunday-style planning on a Friday evening: wrote next week's schedule in her planner with washi tape and packed a rice bowl for Saturday.

Helped at the Lotus Nails front desk from 2 to 5, booking appointments for Hạnh.

lines.what: Got home from the Sunday night Ridgeline shift, ate eggs and rice, and slept until about 1 p.m. at Marisol Gardens unit 132.
First day of fall classes: afternoon section at Bayshore State, Tamsen campus, picking up syllabi for Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Stats 120 and Intro Psych. Fatima saved him a seat.
Checked his savings app and saw the emergency cushion sits near $480 against a $1,200 goal. Packed his bag for the night shift.
Biked to Ridgeline RF-4 for the 10 p.m. outbound night shift.
Finished the shift at 6:30 a.m. and lifted at Iron Flats Fitness at 6:45 before heading home to sleep.
Woke at 1 p.m., skipped class since Tuesday has no section, and did laundry and a grocery run. Arjun mentioned his internship spreadsheet again.
Sent Jade a goodnight text before biking to work for the shift.
Heat wave began. Marcus finished the night shift, where Ridgeline added extra water breaks on the floor.

Ate chicken and rice at home, then biked to Ridgeline in the evening heat.

Thursday afternoon section: took notes during Biomechanics and fought to stay awake in the warm lecture hall.
Had dinner with Arjun at the apartment and listened to him talk applications. Biked to work after.
Payday Friday: after the shift, picked up a Taquería Colima burrito for breakfast.
Lifted at Iron Flats Fitness on a Friday morning in the heat, then slept until early afternoon.
Spent the afternoon at home resting, with Friday off from class. Cooled off by the apartment fan and texted Jade about the weekend.
Saturday morning lift at the gym after his shift, still 100 degrees outside by midday.
Slept through the hottest hours with the fan on high and woke up in the early afternoon.
Saturday date night with Jade at Phở Bến Thành, hot soup despite the heat wave.
Sunday: slept late, then spent the afternoon cleaning his sneakers and straightening the box wall in his closet.
Went over his class syllabi and blocked out Stats 120 homework time for the week.
Rode to Ridgeline for the Sunday 10 p.m. start as the fog returned in the evening.
Labor Day: Marcus works his Sunday-night shift into Monday morning at Ridgeline RF-4, picking totes on the general pick floor at holiday time-and-a-half. Carla walks the floor more than usual.
Rides the bike home from Ridgeline past families setting up picnics at Delgado Park, eats eggs and rice, and sleeps 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. while the college is closed.
Evening at the Marisol Gardens unit with Arjun, who talks about internship applications; Marcus pays his rent share portal reminder and heads out to the 10 p.m. shift.
After the night shift Marcus sleeps 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., then skips the gym and goes over Fatima's shared Ex Phys notes before the week's classes.
At Ridgeline, Noemi's help desk swaps a dead scanner for him, and new tech Bao Tran is shadowing her on his first day.
Reads the breakroom board at 9:40 p.m. for his dock assignment, then clocks in at 10 with Trevor beside him on the floor.
Back from the night shift, sleeps until 1, then takes the Tule Line to Bayshore for the 2 p.m. section, nodding off in Biomechanics.
Quick call with his mom Denise on the train home about her week at the drugstore; she says she is fine.
Heads to Ridgeline for the night shift, listening to old-school West Coast rap in one earbud while picking.
Sleeps after shift, then goes to the 2 p.m. Thursday section at Bayshore and the Stats 120 lecture.
Quick dinner of leftover rice and chicken at home; Arjun suggests he go to bed earlier and Marcus brushes it off.
Thursday night shift at Ridgeline; Trevor complains about rate again while Marcus keeps his phone on a power bank-less battery that dies before 4 a.m.
Payday Friday: after shift Marcus gets a Taquería Colima burrito on Calle Ortega, then sleeps. Ridgeline pays biweekly on Fridays.
Lifts at Iron Flats Fitness in the early evening with Mike's 5/3/1 program, working toward his deadlift goal.
Stays home during the Egrets home opener that draws half the town to the stadium, and texts Jade about her day off before his shift.
Finishes the night shift; Carla hands out conchas to the crew as she does on Saturdays.
Sleeps until early afternoon, then a lift at Iron Flats Fitness and groceries at Ruiz Family Market.
Saturday evening date with Jade at Phở Bến Thành, trying to make up for last night's tension.
Messages the assistant right after his shift at 7 a.m. asking for a cheap high-protein meal prep list for the week, since he can't keep eating random meals.
Sleeps, then cooks his first Sunday chicken-and-rice batch into five containers in the Marisol Gardens kitchen.
Quiet evening with Arjun before heading out to a Sunday-night shift at Ridgeline.

Marcus finishes Sunday night's shift at Ridgeline RF-4 and picks up a power bank at the break room vending kiosk after his phone dies at 4 a.m. again. He eats eggs and rice at Marisol Gardens unit 132 and crashes by 8.
Wakes at 1 p.m., grabs a bag and heads to his 2 p.m. afternoon section at Bayshore State, taking the Tule Line.
Bikes to Ridgeline for the 10 p.m. shift on the general pick floor with Trevor nearby.
After shift at 7 a.m., Marcus asks his assistant for a workable sleep schedule, adding that he doesn't want the 8-hours lecture. He eats eggs and rice and sleeps 8 to 1.
Free Tuesday afternoon: he does laundry, studies Fatima's shared Google Doc notes for Ex Phys, and chats with roommate Arjun in the kitchen.
Bikes to Ridgeline for the night shift; the rear brake squeaks the whole ride.
Gets off shift, then sleeps a short night's day, waking at 1 p.m. for tutoring-free Wednesday; he heads to campus for his 2 p.m. section.
Texts Jade between classes about weekend plans, and she says she wishes he were awake more on her days off.
Evening: Marcus eats a prepped meal and rides to Ridgeline for the shift, listening to West Coast rap in one earbud.
Home at 7 a.m., eats, and sleeps. Wakes at 1 p.m. and rides the Tule Line to his Thursday section.
After class he has a quick gym-less afternoon, calls his mom Denise to check in about her cut hours.
Last night shift of the work week: Carla reminds the crew about rate on the breakroom board and Jose posts assignments at 9:40.
Marcus misses Jade's day off by sleeping through it after the shift, and asks his assistant for a funny text to send her.
Payday Friday: he checks his Ridgeline deposit, pays attention to groceries and bills, and picks up a Taquería Colima burrito on Calle Ortega.
Lifts at Iron Flats Fitness with Mike on the 5/3/1 program before heading home.
Marcus sees the Ridgeline hiring fair crowd on Ruel Road as he leaves shift; Aaliyah Simmons is among the people lined up for seasonal work.
Sleeps through the morning, then does a lazy afternoon at the apartment, cleaning his sneakers.
Saturday evening with Jade at Phở Bến Thành, making up for the missed day off.
Sunday afternoon: Marcus does his chicken-and-rice meal prep, five containers, in the unit 132 kitchen.
Checks his phone and sees Keisha, now AFUSD dispatch, is no longer driving buses, per Rochelle's family chatter online; he mostly scrolls sneaker news.
Bikes to Ridgeline for the Sunday night shift, power bank in his pocket.
Marcus clocked in at Ridgeline RF-4 at 10 p.m. and found José's board posting him to the cold dock, so he borrowed a freezer jacket for the night.
Earlier that day he made the 2 p.m. section on the Bayshore campus and then ate Sunday-prep chicken and rice at the apartment before the shift.
His mom Denise's drugstore hours officially dropped to 24 a week, and she called Marcus to say she was managing fine.
After shift Marcus ate eggs and rice and slept from 8 a.m. until 1 p.m. in unit 132 while Arjun left for the train.
Back at Ridgeline for the night shift, Marcus worked the cold dock again and carpooled nothing, biking in. Trevor griped about rate scanners beeping red.
Marcus got off shift at 6:30 a.m., slept until 1 p.m., then rode the Tule Line to Bayshore for his 2 p.m. section and borrowed Fatima's Google Doc notes for the lecture he missed.
Sunday-through-Thursday night shift on the cold dock; he wore the freezer jacket and listened to old-school West Coast rap in one earbud.
Marcus sat through the Thursday afternoon section half-awake and then grabbed a quick dinner before shift.

Thursday sushi night: Iris ordered as usual and they ate on the couch watching a show on their shared streaming account.
Morning of practice questions and a half-hour of subnetting flashcards.
Swing shift at RF-4; picked up Taquería Colima for her shift meal on Friday as usual.
A busy Friday night with several frozen handhelds; she rebooted and replaced them at the cage.
Walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk in the morning with a coffee.
Went to her parents' fourplex off Vinca to fix the printer and update their phones.
Afternoon study session with the practice app and a long block of port numbers.
Slow Sunday morning; Iris and Noemi went to the Delgado Park harvest farmers market for peppers and stone fruit.
Afternoon study block, then meal prep of rice bowls for the week.
Sunday night co-op survival game with her online squad.
Slept in until 9, then studied her tabbed network guide at the Verdant Commons desk with a practice-test app before leaving for the 2 p.m. swing shift.
Worked the help desk in the cage at RF-4, swapping dead scanner batteries and updating the RMA sheet.
Got home after 10:30 and played the co-op survival game with her squad before bed.
Opened her self-review draft in the morning and cut it down hard, calling it the boss fight, before the self-review deadline that evening.
Taught Bao scanner trigger-board swaps from 3 to 5 p.m. in the cage.
Ate a leftover rice bowl at her desk during the handoff, then handled Carla's text about a dead scanner on the outbound dock.
Late morning at home she did subnetting drills, her weakest topic, and picked up an iced black coffee on the way to work.
Spent the swing shift reimaging laptops and logging tickets in the internal queue, with Greg mostly out of sight in his office.
Watched a show with Iris after shift on their shared streaming account.
Before shift she worked out wording for a short lecture to the night crew about sharing badge PINs.
Trained Bao on scanner repairs from 3 to 5 p.m., then gave the badge PIN talk to the night pickers at handoff.
Got home to Iris's Thursday sushi order.
Ate lunch at home and fixed her parents' printer remotely after her mom called about it.
Greg called the IT desk together and announced he was giving two weeks' notice, leaving Oct 17.
Picked up Taquería Colima for dinner at work as usual on Friday.
Walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk in the morning with her coffee.
Studied network chapters at the desk with the practice-test app for a couple of hours.
Went to dinner with Iris and told her about Greg's notice.
Slept late, then helped her parents at the Vinca Avenue fourplex with a phone problem.
Did subnetting drills and a practice exam in the afternoon.
Played the co-op survival game with her squad in the evening as packetloss_.

Sleeps in until 9 a.m., then drives her hatchback to Ruel Road for the first 10-hour swing of mandatory overtime, 1 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. Spends the evening in the cage clearing a pile of frozen handhelds.
Eats leftover rice bowl at her desk in the IT cage next to the outbound break room and tells Bao the new quota will spike scanner failures.
Morning at home with Iris leaving for work at 8; Noemi studies subnetting for an hour. At Ridgeline she trains Bao on trigger board swaps at 3 p.m.
Evening of many dead scanners and pickers falling behind rate; Carla calls her cell about three dead units on the outbound dock.
Late morning she sketches a plain-language guide for night pickers on rebooting frozen handhelds and asks her assistant to help write it in plain English and Spanish.
Swing shift: tapes printed reboot guides near the outbound break room and walks a few pickers through the steps. Candidate forum talk about warehouse growth buzzes in the break room.
Studies for the cert with the practice-test app before shift, missing a handful of port-number questions.
Trains Bao on scanner repairs 3-5 p.m., then works the rest of the 10-hour swing. Iris orders Thursday sushi, saved for her to eat after midnight.
Fills up at the Ruel Road station and grabs Taquería Colima for her Friday shift meal.
Heavy Friday swing with scanner RMAs piling up; she updates the RMA sheet after hours and logs desk tickets.
Walks the Ulloa marsh boardwalk in the morning, then works her every-other-Saturday overtime shift at Ridgeline.
On break she forwards Iris's suggested study calendar to her assistant and asks it to be tweaked around overtime days.
Visits her parents' fourplex off Vinca Avenue, fixes the printer, and her brother Mateo asks for help building his first PC for his December birthday.
Spends a quiet afternoon on subnetting drills with the study guide, then plays the co-op survival game with her squad as packetloss_.
Slept in on the holiday, then walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk with Iris, who had the day off for Indigenous Peoples' Day, before a coffee run.
Worked the 1 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. swing in the IT cage at RF-4, clearing frozen handhelds as peak overtime kept the scanners busy.
Got home near midnight, ate leftover rice bowl and did 20 minutes of subnetting in the practice app.
Slept until 9, fixed her parents' printer remotely over a quick call, then drove to Ruel Road, gas first at the station.
Trained Bao on scanner trigger boards from 3 to 5, then a director email arrived demanding a root cause for dead batteries by end of day; she vented to her assistant and had her reply made less rude.
Late shift stretched on with a red-beep night as scanners failed and pickers fell behind rate; Carla texted her about dead units.
Midterm week crowds everywhere; Noemi spent her late morning on the cert practice questions at home, weak on port numbers.
Swing shift in the cage, logging tickets and updating the RMA sheet for scanners headed back to the vendor.
Late dinner at home with Iris, who talked about the shared budget sheet.
Slept in, then Thursday sushi night prep with Iris; Iris ordered as usual.
Trained Bao 3 to 5 on the repair bench; word spread that Greg's last day was tomorrow.
Greg handed her a short list of vendor tickets and passwords for the RMA portal at the end of the evening.
Greg's last day; Rhonda's team announced Victor as acting IT desk lead, and Noemi absorbed Greg's vendor tickets, scanner RMAs and scheduling on the spot.
Told her assistant Victor 'got the loot drop' and asked for help drafting a congrats message to him.
Picked up Taquería Colima for her Friday shift meal and ate it in the cage while building the new schedule.
Walked the marsh boardwalk in the morning, then coffee with Iris.
Worked her alternating Saturday at RF-4 handling scanner repairs and the new vendor ticket queue.
Late night at home on her desktop, unwinding with a gaming session.
Slept late, then did two hours of subnetting drills with the study guide.
Helped her brother Mateo plan parts for his first PC at her parents' fourplex.
Sunday night co-op survival game with her online squad as packetloss_.
Late morning at the Verdant Commons kitchen table, Noemi asks for help writing a short email to Rhonda that 'mentions' she's covering Greg's duties without asking for anything.
Before shift she moves her network cert exam from Nov 8 to Saturday Dec 6 because the overtime leaves no study time.
On the 1 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. swing at RF-4, Rhonda replies in the IT cage that the permanent lead decision comes after peak, mid-December.
Late night at home, Iris is still up and Noemi tells her about the timeline over reheated rice.
Slow morning at home, Noemi calls this 'hardcore mode' week and asks for a meal-prep list for the 10-hour swings.
At RF-4 she spends the afternoon in the cage on dead scanners, with the ~30-handheld pile at peak.
Carla texts Noemi's cell about a dead scanner on the outbound dock mid-shift.
Noemi sleeps in until nine, then does a block of subnetting flashcards with coffee before shift.
She stops by Ana's office at RF-4 and learns Ana handles the internal lead posting paperwork.
Evening swing: a run of frozen handhelds on the floor keeps her moving.
Wakes late and updates her RMA sheet at home, listing scanners to send back to the vendor.
Afternoon training with Bao in the cage on trigger-board swaps.
Iris orders Thursday sushi and Noemi eats it at midnight after work.
Fills up at the Ruel Road station and has Taquería Colima tacos for the Friday meal at her desk.
She submits her application for the permanent IT desk lead through Ana's posting process.
Evening on the floor, Victor's acting-lead mess slows her down on a vendor ticket; she works late.
Saturday morning walk on the Ulloa marsh boardwalk before her overtime Saturday.
Works the every-other-Saturday overtime shift at RF-4, mostly scanner triage.
Home late, she and Iris watch a show on their shared streaming account.
Sunday late morning she runs subnetting drills and asks for harder problems.
Visits her parents' fourplex off Vinca Avenue and fixes the printer.
Sunday night she plays her co-op survival game as packetloss_ with her squad.
Slept in until 9, then studied subnetting at the kitchen table in the Verdant Commons apartment while Iris was at work.

Filled up at the Ruel Road station and drove 9 minutes to start her 1 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. overtime swing. Ana from HR told her the temporary lead-duties differential kicks in this pay period, bringing her to $31.90 an hour.
Spent the evening in the cage triaging dead scanners and updating the RMA sheet, with Bao handling battery swaps.
Quiet morning, then drove to work for the 1 p.m. swing. Trained Bao on scanner repairs from 3 to 5 in the cage.
Carla texted her cell about three dead scanners on the outbound dock; Noemi walked over and swapped them out.
Got home near midnight and ate leftover rice with Iris, who was still up with the budget sheet.
Studied port numbers with the practice-test app before shift.
Worked the overtime swing, handling a battery batch problem and some badge reader tickets.
On a break she got a breach alert email about an old shopping account and realized she used the same password on it as on nearly everything personal.
Iris and Noemi talked at breakfast about her old resume, last touched in 2022. Noemi hesitated to list the lead-coverage work as her own.
Drove in for the swing and trained Bao on scanner repairs from 3 to 5. Victor passed along a vendor ticket on his way out.
Late in the shift, she and Bao cleared the cage backlog.
Worked the overtime swing on Halloween. Pickers in costume jokes aside, several handhelds froze mid-shift.
Got Taquería Colima for shift dinner, her Friday habit.
Got home after 11:30, and Iris had left candy from the apartment's trick-or-treaters on the counter.
Spent Saturday morning migrating personal accounts into a password manager, working through the list from Wednesday's breach scare, with a checklist to track which accounts were done.
Short walk on the Ulloa marsh boardwalk, careful of slick planks.
Afternoon subnetting drills at the home desk.
Slept late, then went through the last of the password manager imports.
Iris dropped hints about their Nov 15 anniversary; Noemi asked which restaurant Iris would pick and booked a Calle Ortega dinner for 7 p.m.
Sunday night co-op survival game with her online squad as packetloss_.
Slept until 9, then a slow morning with Iris before she left for the dental office; Noemi did a round of subnetting drills at the kitchen counter.
Ten-hour swing at RF-4 in the IT cage; Bao handled battery swaps while Noemi worked through the repair backlog and updated the RMA sheet.
Carla texted Noemi's cell about two dead scanners on the outbound dock near the end of shift; Noemi swapped them out before the handoff.
Election day: Noemi voted at the Vinca Avenue Community Center on the way to work, with Iris along.
Swing shift at RF-4 with Bao in the cage; the Tue 3-5 training block covered scanner trigger boards.
Got home after 11:30, ate leftover rice with Iris, and watched the election chatter before bed.

Late morning, Noemi began looking at network tech openings outside Ridgeline, including St. Anselm IT, and asked her assistant for job-posting keywords, joking that she was just checking other servers.
Worked the swing shift, filling in for lead duties on vendor tickets and scheduling while Victor was on days.
Told Iris she was sending out applications; they talked it over late at the kitchen table.
Drafted a reply to an email from Victor and rewrote it three times to strip out the sarcasm before sending.
Swing shift in the cage; Thursday training with Bao from 3 to 5 on battery contacts.
Iris's Thursday sushi was waiting when Noemi got home; they ate it after her shift.
Morning of practice-test questions, then a quick check on the job applications she had started.
Picked up Taquería Colima for her Friday shift meal and ate it in the IT cage next to the outbound break room.
Red-beep night on the outbound dock: many scanners failed and pickers fell behind rate, so Noemi spent the shift swapping units.
Walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk in the morning, careful on the damp planks.
Worked the every-other-Saturday overtime shift at RF-4.
Home late, a quick chat with Iris, then collapsed.
Slept in, then helped her parents with their printer at the Vinca fourplex and saw her brother Mateo.
Afternoon study session with the tabbed guide and subnetting problems.
Sunday night co-op survival game with her online squad as packetloss_.

Noemi sleeps in until 9, then does a Monday study block at the kitchen table at Verdant Commons. Her latest practice exam run averages 80% after the subnetting drills, the first time she is over the pass line.
Shares the 80% result and asks what to drill next. This is a one-off check-in on a good score, with the exam already moved to Dec 6 because of overtime weeks ago.
Drives the 9 minutes to Ruel Road for the 1 p.m. ten-hour swing and stops at the Ruel Road station for gas first. She spends the afternoon in the cage on the scanner pile.
Works late covering Greg's old duties, including vendor tickets and updating the RMA sheet. Gets home after 11:30 and winds down.
Veterans Day: Ridgeline runs as usual, so Noemi has a slow morning with Iris, who has the day off from the dental office, before her swing.
Spends the early afternoon on subnetting drills, then works the 1 p.m. swing and trains Bao on battery swaps and trigger boards from 3 to 5.
A busy night with several handhelds failing, a red-beep night, and Carla texts her about dead scanners on the outbound floor.
Late morning at home, Noemi drafts a cover letter for outside network tech roles and asks for help with it. She wants the line to say she 'supported the team' instead of 'ran the desk during peak'.
Drives to the 1 p.m. swing. The cage is stacked with scanners and Acting Victor is out of the office again.
Eats a leftover rice bowl at her desk and gets in a few port-number flashcards between tickets.
Gets home after the shift. Iris has left the budget sheet open on the table, and Noemi checks the December trip savings.
The first fall storm hits and rain floods Ruel Road. Noemi's usual 9-minute drive takes much longer around the potholes and standing water.
Wet totes and water-damaged scanners flood the cage. She and Bao dry out and test units through the shift.
Iris orders sushi as usual on Thursday and saves Noemi a box to eat when she gets in past 11:30.
The storm continues and Noemi wakes to rain, pushing her morning study block to a mock quiz on ports.
Works the swing and picks up Taquería Colima for her Friday shift meal on the way in.
Another wet red-beep night with many scanners going down, and she works with Carla and a shift lead to replace them quickly.
It is the three-year anniversary. Noemi skips the boardwalk because the planks are slick in November and sleeps in.
Works her Saturday overtime shift this week and fixes scanners in the cage until the afternoon.
Dinner at a Calle Ortega restaurant at 7 p.m. for their anniversary, as booked.
Sunday morning at her parents' fourplex off Vinca fixing her mom's phone and the printer while Mateo asks about PC parts.
An afternoon study session of subnetting drills and practice tests at home.
Plays the co-op survival game on her ultrawide with her online squad as packetloss_.
Slept until 9, then walked the Ulloa marsh boardwalk loosely before heading to Ruel Road; started the 1 p.m. ten-hour swing in the IT cage fixing frozen handhelds.
Updated her RMA sheet during the evening rush and covered Greg's old vendor tickets.
Got home after 11:30, ate leftover rice with Iris and did a few subnetting drills before bed.
Slept in, then went through Iris's shared budget sheet and brainstormed gift ideas for the Nov 15 anniversary follow-up, wanting something that fits Iris's love of lists.
Tuesday shift on Ruel Road; trained Bao on scanner trigger boards from 3 to 5.
Late-night red-beep stretch as pickers fell behind rate; Carla texted about dead scanners.
Midday study session with the practice-test app and tabbed guide before shift.
Worked the swing shift in the cage, tracking scanner RMAs and handling scheduling.
Came home late and played a bit on her desktop before sleeping.
Quick morning at home, then to Ruel Road; Thursday training block with Bao from 3 to 5.
Iris's Thursday sushi was waiting when she got home past 11:30.
Did subnetting drills before bed.
Friday shift; grabbed Taquería Colima for dinner break.
Fixed a batch of frozen handhelds as the overtime week wound down.
Drove home after 11:30 along quiet Ruel Road.
Slept until 9, then walked the marsh boardwalk Saturday morning, avoiding the slick planks.
Spent the afternoon at her parents' fourplex off Vinca fixing a printer, with the food drive crowds around town.
Evening at home with Iris, planning December trip savings.
Slow Sunday morning, then a long practice exam session with the study guide.
Helped with groceries and laundry in the unit with Iris.
Sunday night co-op game with her online squad as packetloss_.

principals.name: Rafael Henríquez
principals.role: automotive technology student at Tamsen Valley College, helps run the family pupusa stand

lines.what: Slept in a bit before the semester's first Monday. Helped Gladys load the cooler and canopy back into the garage after the weekend stand, then did the brakes lab prep reading at the kitchen table.
Drove the Tacoma to Tamsen Valley College for the first brakes lab, which was only a walkthrough of the bay and safety rules, 8-11.
Evening pickup soccer at Delgado Park, then watched an engine teardown video before bed.

Fall term began at Tamsen Valley. Circled Lot C twice, gave up and parked on the street, then sat through the first engine performance class 1-4 with Roberto Salas going over grading and bay cleanliness.
After class Dante floated his idea of flipping used Civics from auctions again over horchata.
Helped Oscar check the generator oil in the driveway before bed.
Brakes lab 8-11 in the heat wave; the bay was stifling and the instructor added water breaks while they pulled drums.
Grabbed lunch at home, then drove Ximena to her cosmetology class because her Corolla's AC was weak, and looked it over in the lot.
Stayed in at night with a fan on, watching teardown videos.
Engine performance 1-4 at Tamsen Valley with Salas, stuck in the heat; they studied compression testing.
Thursday stand shift 5-10 p.m. at the Delgado Park lot setup, running the griddle with the generator in the heat.
Dulce texted that Efraín is putting her on Fridays; Rafael agreed to pick her up.
Worked out his Friday route in his head and with Gladys so he'd leave the stand in time to reach Colima by 9 and Dulce wouldn't wait outside alone.
Worked the stand through the evening in the heat, griddle going nonstop.
Picked Dulce up from Taquería Colima at 9 p.m. and drove her home to Marisol Gardens, Mexican Coke in the cupholder.
Slept late, then did the Saturday stand shift with Ximena helping on the griddle.
Filled the Tacoma at the Ruel Road station and checked the slow oil leak.
Late evening walk with Ximena after the heat broke, talking about someday having a shop.
Sunday morning helped Oscar and Gladys run the stand at the Delgado Park farmers market 8-2.
Family meal from day-old bread and leftover pupusas, then broke down the canopy.
Late night skimmed the engine performance syllabus and set out the week's clothes.
Labor Day, no classes. Rafael sleeps in, then spends the morning under the Taco's hood checking the slow oil leak with a flashlight.
Afternoon at Delgado Park with his parents and Ximena for the Labor Day picnic, plus pickup soccer in the evening.
Late evening he watches an engine teardown video before bed.
Brakes lab runs 8 to 11 at Tamsen Valley with Dante as his lab partner, since Monday was a holiday and the class moved.
Engine performance with Roberto Salas, 1 to 4. Salas docks points for a messy bay during the teardown.
Evening he fills the Taco at the Ruel Road station and grabs a Mexican Coke.
Brakes lab 8 to 11, then a quick lunch at home. He brings Gladys a new hose clamp for the generator.
Evening he does the Wednesday prep for the stand, then watches teardown videos.
Engine performance 1 to 4 with Salas. Dante pitches the Civic-flipping idea again over lunch.
Thursday stand shift at the Delgado Park lot. He runs the griddle for the evening crowd.
Rafael helps Gladys prep masa and curtido. He picks up pork at Ruiz Family Market from Chuy at the family price.
Friday stand shift, and he leaves to pick up Dulce at Colima at 9. The football opener traffic slows the drive.
Saturday at the stand with Ximena helping. The line is steady and he sets up the canopy.
Gladys brings day-old bread from Lupe's bakery for the family meal. Rafael eats a revuelta pupusa with extra curtido.
Sunday market at Delgado Park, 8 to 2. Luz parks the elote cart nearby and they trade jokes.
Afternoon he tears down the canopy and tests the practice questions on his phone, but gets tired and stops after a few.
Evening at home he talks over next week's schedule with Oscar and checks the Taco before bed.
Rafael has brakes lab at Tamsen Valley College from 8 to 11, then helps Gladys pick up masa supplies at Ruiz Family Market, where Chuy gives the family price on pork shoulder.
Evening pickup soccer at Delgado Park, then he watches engine teardown videos in bed on his cracked phone at 20% battery.
Engine performance with Salas from 1 to 4; Dante pitches his Tuesday salvage auction picks again during the lab break.
Fills the Tacoma at the Ruel Road station for about $50 and drives home along Pell Road, then studies G1 chapter headings for the first practice quiz.
Brakes lab in the morning, then takes the first G1 practice quiz on his laptop at the school library and scores 58%. He blanked and changed three right answers to wrong ones.
Late morning he texts the assistant a refrigerant handling question from the quiz, saying he knows it on the car but not in the words.
Eats a quiet dinner at home with Oscar and Gladys, who ask how class went. He says fine and does not mention the score.
Asks the assistant for help wording a request to reschedule a brakes-lab makeup so it will not collide with his Thursday stand shift.
Engine performance with Salas from 1 to 4, then helps Oscar load the canopy and generator for the Thursday stand.
Runs the griddle through the evening stand shift and teardown, home late.
Skips nothing in the morning but sleeps badly; he reviews flashcard notes between classes and has lunch at the college.
Works the Friday stand evening, then at 9 p.m. picks up Dulce from Taquería Colima and drives her home to Marisol Gardens.
Sees the Ridgeline hiring fair line on Ruel Road while driving to the stand and honks at a friend in it, but does not stop.
Saturday stand shift with Ximena helping; she asks if he has thought about the shop dream.
Teardown at night and bed past midnight.
Sunday market stand at Delgado Park from 8 to 2, with Luz selling elotes nearby.
Afternoon nap, then a family dinner at home.
Plans to retry the G1 material and looks up flashcard ideas before bed.
Brakes lab at Tamsen Valley College 8-11, then lunch in the truck and a quick shop-floor cleanup. Evening pickup soccer at Delgado Park.
Home in the ranch house off Pell Road, he watched an engine teardown video before bed.
Engine performance class with Salas 1-4, where Rafael's bay got a cleanliness check. Afterward he heard Dulce's mom Yesenia say the hospital was chaos with the new charting system going live.
Evening at home helping Gladys prep masa tubs and checking the generator.
Brakes lab 8-11, then a stop at Ruiz Family Market where Chuy set aside pork shoulder for Oscar.
Drove Ximena to a cosmetology class and checked her Corolla's tires.

The Taco's battery light flickered on the drive to class and the headlights dimmed at a red light; he diagnosed a failing alternator. He compared three alternator prices and picked a rebuilt one to save $80.
Engine performance 1-4, then worked the Thursday stand shift on the griddle at Delgado Park prep and teardown.
Told the assistant over text the alternator whined, the voltage read low and the lights dimmed under load, then asked what the textbook calls that symptom.
Worked the Friday stand shift, then picked up Dulce from Taquería Colima at 9 p.m. so she wasn't waiting outside.
Worked the family booth at the Calle Ortega Street Fair, running the griddle all afternoon through crowds and music.
Teardown of the canopy and generator after the fair, then a pan dulce from Lupe at Las Hermanas.
Sunday stand shift at the Delgado Park market 8-2.
Afternoon nap, then planned the rebuilt alternator install for the lab.
Brakes lab 8-11 at Tamsen Valley College, then lunch in the truck with a torta; the Taco's battery light flickered on the drive in.
Pickup soccer at Delgado Park in the evening with friends, then home to Pell Road.
Watched engine teardown videos in bed before midnight.
Quiet morning at home helping Gladys carry masa buckets, then a stop at Ruiz Family Market for pork with Chuy's family price.
Studied G1 flashcards-style rereading in the truck between errands.
Dinner with his parents and an early night.
Brakes lab 8-11, where Dante pitched his Tuesday auction Civic flipping again and mentioned a car going cheap.
Lost a set of Dante's borrowed sockets and agreed to pay him $120. Later, from the truck at a red light, asked the assistant whether Dante's auction-flip math is realistic.
Evening at home, texted Ximena about the weekend and watched teardown videos.
Engine performance with Salas 1-4; his bay got docked a few points for an unclean bench.
Thursday stand shift at Delgado Park prep, setting up canopy and generator and running the griddle for the evening.
Teardown and cleanup, then bed late.
Morning errands and parts shopping for a rebuilt alternator, planning to fix the truck in lab Saturday.
Friday stand shift, then left to pick Dulce up from Taquería Colima at 9.
Dulce told him on the ride about her friend group blowing up after Brianna's breakup with Tyler.
Installed the rebuilt alternator in the school lab himself for $95.
After doing his own truck, asked the assistant how to bleed Ximena's Corolla brakes, then did it at her place.
Saturday stand shift with Ximena helping.
Sunday Delgado Park harvest market, running the griddle 8-2 among families and seniors after church.
Family lunch from leftover pupusas, then teardown and a nap.
Evening at home with a quick scroll of G1 notes and bed by midnight.
Brakes lab at Tamsen Valley 8-11, then lunch in the truck and a bit of chapter reading before heading home.
Filled up the Tacoma at the Ruel Road station, then helped Gladys and Oscar run through supplies for the stand.
Pickup soccer at Delgado Park Monday evening with friends.
Watched engine teardown videos in bed until midnight.
Quiet morning at home, then drove to Tamsen Valley for the afternoon.
Engine performance class 1-4 with Salas, working on a misfire diagnosis with Dante.
Dante mentioned the Tuesday salvage auction again while they cleaned the bay.
Ate dinner with his parents and talked about moving the stand on Saturday.
Brakes lab 8-11, then a stop at Ruiz Family Market with Gladys for stand groceries.
Serviced the stand's generator in the driveway before the move.
Evening at home reading the G1 chapter and getting frustrated with the wording.
Morning class prep, then engine performance 1-4 with Salas.
Asked the assistant to turn the chapter into short spoken flashcards he could record as voice memos.
Thursday stand shift at the Delgado lot, listening to flashcards while prepping the griddle.
Brakes lab and a quick lunch with Ximena on campus.
Friday evening at the stand packing up early to drive Dulce home from Colima at 9.
Helped load the truck bed with the canopy poles for tomorrow.
Moved the canopy, generator and griddle to the Ruel Road gas station lot and set up for the first night, with Oscar and Gladys.
Luz stayed at the Delgado market and stopped by to wish them luck on the move.
Got home late and stayed up drafting a setup checklist for his parents instead of studying.
Slept in, then helped Gladys with masa and curtido at the house.
Sunday evening shift at the Ruel Road lot, using the new checklist.
Played voice-memo flashcards in the truck on the drive home.
Brakes lab at Tamsen Valley College 8-11, then lunch and a drive home in the Tacoma. Evening pickup soccer at Delgado Park.
Recorded a few voice-memo flashcards in the truck, then watched engine teardown videos before bed.
Tuesday morning helped Oscar load the generator and griddle gear at the house, then drove to campus for engine performance 1-4 with Salas.
Listened to flashcard memos while prepping the griddle at home, then texted Ximena about the weekend.
Brakes lab 8-11 at Tamsen Valley, then filled the Taco at the Ruel Road station, noticing the traffic from Ridgeline's new overtime shifts.
Gladys mentioned the candidate forum at the community center where people argue about Ruel Road potholes and warehouses; Rafael skipped it to help prep masa containers for the stand.
Late evening watched a teardown video of a Honda engine.
Engine performance 1-4 with Salas, then lunch with Dante, who pitched buying more auction Civics. Rafael wondered how many cars he could sell before needing a dealer license.
Asked the assistant whether he needs a dealer license to sell more than a few cars a year.
Thursday stand shift at the Ruel Road lot area running the griddle, with setup and teardown of canopy and generator.
Morning brakes review, then fixed a loose battery terminal on the Taco before the afternoon.
Evening at the Ruel Road stand. At 8:50 he left to pick up Dulce from Taquería Colima and got back by 9:20.
Saturday stand shift with Ximena helping. Gladys worried about the lot after dark.
Midday bought pork for chicharrón from Chuy at Ruiz Family Market for the family.
Sunday errands in the morning and a quiet breakfast with his parents. Oscar and Gladys talked about the week's sales.
Sunday evening stand shift 5-10 p.m., then voice-memo flashcards while breaking down the canopy.
Indigenous Peoples' Day, no classes at Tamsen Valley. Rafael sleeps in, then services the stand's 3500W generator in the driveway off Pell Road.
Afternoon at Delgado Park for pickup soccer with friends, then a ride home in the Taco with horchata.
Late evening he watches engine teardown videos in bed and studies his voice-memo flashcards for the G1.
Tuesday engine performance with Salas from 1 to 4 at Tamsen Valley, diagnosing a misfire on a lab Civic.

lines.what: Thao gets home from her night shift on 4 West, rides the nurse shuttle down Ortega Hill, and finds an email confirming the paid 8-hour charting class for Sept 9.
Sleeps 8:30 to 3 with the blackout curtains and box fan, while Vinca traffic backs up outside for the first day of school.
Makes cà phê sữa đá in the thermos and walks the Ulloa marsh boardwalk loop before heading to her night shift.

Skips Hạnh's 1 p.m. call mid-sleep and finds another Vietnamese voicemail later.

Sunday dinner at Hạnh's house with Linh, who talks about starting classes.
